title: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)

sections.label: Singapore net zero emissions reduction
sections.summary: Singapore must cut net emissions per person by 8.31 tonnes by 2050, mainly from power, industry and transport, and will receive up to 100 megawatts of Lao hydropower.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In order to achieve net zero, Singapore needs to reduce the net output of each person by 8.31 tonnes of carbon emissions by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This reduction needs to come from the power, industrial and transport sectors, which account for more than 97% of our total primary emissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Up to 100 megawatts of renewable hydropower from Lao PDR will be delivered to Singapore via interconnections with Thailand and Malaysia.

sections.label: Third National Climate Change Study
sections.summary: The Centre for Climate Research Singapore released the Third National Climate Change Study, estimating more extreme projections for Singapore's weather and sea level rise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: In January this year, the Centre for Climate Research Singapore released the Third National Climate Change Study, which estimated more extreme projections for Singapore's weather conditions, including temperature, humidity, rainfall, wind speeds, and sea level rise.

sections.label: Tuas Mega Port investment
sections.summary: Singapore is the world's second busiest port, maritime contributes 7% of GDP and employs over 170,000 people, and $20 billion is invested in Tuas Mega Port.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Today, Singapore is the second busiest port in the world and with the maritime industry contributing to 7% of local GDP, employing more than 170,000 people, the investment of $20 billion into the Tuas Mega Port can be seen as a vote of confidence in the development of Singapore's port capabilities as an economic strategy.

sections.label: Northern Sea Route cargo growth
sections.summary: Cargo along the Northern Sea Route rose from 41,000 tonnes in 2010 to 285,000 tonnes in 2019 and is expected to increase as the Arctic warms faster.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Cargo passage along the Northern Sea Route has increased from 41,000 tonnes of cargo in 2010 to 285,000 tonnes in 2019 and is expected to only increase in the future, given that the warming in the Arctic has been four times faster than the rest of the world.

sections.label: Singapore regional green finance
sections.summary: At the World Climate Action Summit, Singapore announced plans to raise S$6.6 billion to finance efforts to green the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At the World Climate Action Summit, Singapore led the charge on regional partnerships by announcing plans to raise S$6.6 billion to finance efforts to green the region.

sections.label: Revised 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution
sections.summary: The Government committed to reducing emissions to around 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2030 after peaking earlier, under the revised 2030 NDC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In addition, the Government has also committed to reducing emissions to around 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (MtCO2e) in 2030 after peaking emissions earlier as part of the revised 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC).

sections.label: Future Energy Fund infrastructure use
sections.summary: Asks how the $5 billion Future Energy Fund will support essential infrastructure, especially long-gestation areas like nuclear energy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How will the $5 billion Future Energy Fund be used to support the development of essential infrastructure especially those with long gestation periods like nuclear energy?

sections.label: Green Finance Action Plan update
sections.summary: Asks for an update on the Green Finance Action Plan and other sector initiatives using Singapore's hub position, and their effect on competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Government give an update on the Green Finance Action Plan?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While mandating sustainable aviation fuel for departing flights is a commendable way, what other strategic initiatives are planned across different sectors to leverage on our hub position?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How will such initiatives affect Singapore's economic competitiveness as a travel hub?

sections.label: Worst-case temperature scenario
sections.summary: In a worst-case scenario of rapidly rising global emissions, Singapore could face daily maximum temperatures above 35°C almost year-round.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: In the worst-case scenario, where global emissions continue rising rapidly, Singapore could face daily maximum temperatures exceeding 35°C almost year-round.

sections.label: Enhanced climate targets announced
sections.summary: In 2022 Singapore announced enhanced climate targets: cut 2030 emissions to 60 million tonnes after peaking earlier, and net zero by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: In 2022, we announced our enhanced climate targets, committing to reduce emissions by 2030 to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, after peaking emissions earlier; and to achieve net zero emissions by 2050.

sections.label: Carbon tax raised
sections.summary: The carbon tax was raised to $25 per tonne this year and is a key enabler.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Our carbon tax, which was raised to $25 per tonne this year, is a key enabler.

sections.label: Future Energy Fund set up
sections.summary: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked how Singapore can use emerging technologies for its energy transition; a $5 billion Future Energy Fund will be set up this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked how Singapore can capitalise on emerging technologies to support our energy transition.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: This year, the Government will set up a Future Energy Fund (FEF) with an initial injection of $5 billion.

sections.label: bbp energy savings support
sections.summary: Using Enterprise Singapore's Enterprise Development Grant and scale-up programmes, bbp helped businesses achieve over $90 million in energy savings and avoid 240,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions across nine Asian markets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Leveraging Enterprise Singapore’s Enterprise Development Grant and other scale-up programmes, bbp has helped businesses achieve more than $90 million of energy savings and avoid 240,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions, across nine Asian markets.

sections.label: Asia climate investment needs
sections.summary: Asia will require an estimated US$1.7 trillion in climate and infrastructure investment annually through to 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Asia will require an estimated US$1.7 trillion dollars in climate and infrastructure investment annually through to 2030.

sections.label: FAST-P blended finance launch
sections.summary: At COP28, a new blended finance initiative, Financing Asia's Transition Partnerships, was announced to mobilise up to US$5 billion to de-risk and finance green projects in Asia.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: As an example, at COP28, I announced the launch of a new blended finance initiative – the Financing Asia’s Transition Partnerships (FAST-P) that will mobilise up to US$5 billion from public and private sector partners to de-risk and finance transition and marginally bankable green projects in Asia.

sections.label: IEA Regional Cooperation Centre Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore will establish the first International Energy Agency Regional Cooperation Centre outside its Paris headquarters to support regional energy transition.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: To support regional energy transition, we will establish in Singapore the first-ever International Energy Agency Regional Cooperation Centre outside of its Paris headquarters.

sections.label: Singapore-Japan green shipping corridor
sections.summary: In December 2023, Singapore signed a memorandum of cooperation with Japan to establish the Singapore-Japan Green and Digital Shipping corridor, complementing partnerships with the Netherlands, China and the US.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: In December 2023, we signed a memorandum of cooperation with Japan to establish the Singapore-Japan Green and Digital Shipping corridor.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: This complements similar partnerships with ports in the Netherlands, China and the United States (US), allowing us to support the decarbonisation, digitalisation and growth of the maritime industry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I have explained why it is in Singapore's interest to commit to climate action, outlined concrete steps we are taking as a nation to meet our ambitious climate targets, and highlighted how Singapore is stepping up to encourage regional and global action.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We must stay the course in our green transition because we want to leave behind a liveable, resilient and thriving country and world for future generations of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Mature workers and caregivers employment
sections.summary: A study found Singapore's labour market is predicted to tighten, with barriers and drivers affecting mature workers and women with caregiving duties, who are untapped groups to supplement a shrinking local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The key insights are that in the next five years, Singapore's labour market is predicted to tighten with unemployment and retrenchments expected to stabilise in the longer term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The study found that there are barriers and drivers that enable mature workers and women with caregiving duties to find and stay in employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We opine that other than automation, mature workers and women with caregiving responsibilities are untapped groups to supplement a shrinking local workforce.

sections.label: Total fertility rate fall
sections.summary: Singapore's total fertility rate has fallen to a historic 1.04.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Our total fertility rate (TFR) has fallen to a historic 1.04.

sections.label: Elective egg freezing uptake
sections.summary: The passage asks what the uptake of elective egg freezing has been since 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What is the uptake of elective egg freezing since 2023?

sections.label: Population projections clarification
sections.summary: The Government clarified it does not aim for a 10 million population and anticipates significantly below 6.9 million by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Government has clarified that it does not aim for Singapore's population to increase to 10 million, and it is anticipating a population of significantly below 6.9 million by 2030.

sections.label: All-time low fertility rate
sections.summary: The most worrying statistic released was the all-time low fertility rate of 1.04.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The most worrying statistic released was the all-time low fertility rate of 1.04.

sections.label: Migrant domestic workers for elderly
sections.summary: The passage asks the projected number of migrant domestic workers needed for the ageing population, noting falling TFR's negative impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With an increasing number of elderly who may be frail who need help to look after them, what is the projected numbers of migrant domestic workers (MDWs) required to support and meet the needs of our ageing population?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our falling TFR will have a negative impact on the future of our society and economy.

sections.label: Marriage and parenthood support
sections.summary: In 2022 the TFR hit 1.04 and citizen births fell 4%, with five-year averages lower than the preceding five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On supporting marriage and parenthood, Mr Chairman, several hon Members of this House have already mentioned that in 2022, our TFR hit another low of 1.04 and there was also a 4% reduction in citizen births from the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although we have seen an encouraging increase in citizen marriages over the past two years, the annual average number of marriages and births over the last five years remains lower than that of the preceding five years.

sections.label: Young Singaporeans marriage views poll
sections.summary: An IPS pre-conference poll found seven in 10 young Singaporeans aged 21 to 34 believe marriage is not necessary, though most still want to marry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in a recent pre-conference poll done by the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) for the Singapore Perspective Conference 2024, seven in 10 of young Singaporeans aged between 21 and 34 believe that it is not necessary to get married, but most still want to do so.

sections.label: Employees accept lower pay FWA
sections.summary: Research has shown that employees are willing to work for less pay with flexible work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Research has already shown that employees are willing to work for less pay with FWA.

sections.label: Caregivers prefer flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: A survey of nearly 3,000 caregivers found close to 90% chose FWAs as their most preferred support, with NTUC advocating FWAs since 1995.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In a recent survey by the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) Women and Family Unit and the PAP Women's Wing, close to 90% of nearly 3,000 caregivers surveyed chose FWAs as their most preferred form of support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The NTUC has been advocating for FWAs since 1995, when we introduced FWAs in our collective agreement negotiations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We are also heartened to note that there are over 12,000 companies – mostly SMEs – which are signatories to the 2017 Tripartite Standards for FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: During COVID-19, introductions of FWAs in companies spiked with Singaporean firms offering FWAs rising up to 70% from 53% pre-COVID-19.

sections.label: Childcare leave ends at age 12
sections.summary: Under current regulations, childcare leave ends when a child turns 12, assuming they are independent by then.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Chairman, under current regulations, childcare leave ends when a child turns 12 – assuming they are independent by then.

sections.label: Timeline for paternity leave mandate
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Government can provide a firm timeline on when the extra two weeks of paternity leave will be mandated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Government provide a firm timeline on when the extra two weeks of paternity leave will be mandated?

sections.label: Lactation room floor area rule
sections.summary: Under the Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment, lactation rooms are required only for buildings above 10,000 square meters, less than 10% of over 4,000 offices and business parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment, lactation rooms are only required for buildings with a floor area of above 10,000 square meters – this is less than 10% of more than 4,000 offices and business parks.

sections.label: Code lactation room inclusivity
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will lower the GFA threshold for lactation rooms and mandate more of them in the next Code update.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Designing our public facilities for families sends a visible and clear signal that this is a Singapore made for families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It has been more than five years since the Code was last updated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Government make our Code more inclusive in the next iteration of the Code by lowering the gross floor area (GFA) threshold for the requirement of lactation rooms and also mandating more lactation rooms in buildings – the same way we do for accessible toilets?

sections.label: Paternity and childcare leave
sections.summary: Asks how the Government is considering measures such as more childcare leave for both parents, given companies rebalancing remote work days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The ability to be present as the main caregiver of their children is one of the main wants of every parent and this, of course, includes daddies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I therefore applaud the Government's willingness to adapt to changing times by increasing paternity leave allowances, yet even that may not be quite enough as companies have been observed to be "rebalancing", by calibrating the number of remote working days allowed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Therefore, I ask: how is the Government looking into other measures such as increasing the number of childcare leave for both mummies and daddies in response, to ensure that both parents are able to witness every important milestone of their children?

sections.label: Baby Bonus cash and CDA
sections.summary: Asks whether the Baby Bonus cash gift quantum will be reviewed for inflation and whether CDA approved uses can be widened.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With regard to the Baby Bonus Scheme, will the quantum of the cash gift be periodically reviewed to be aligned with inflation?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And can the Ministry explore widening the list of approved uses for the Child Development Account (CDA) to further assist parents with child-related expenses?

sections.label: Total population by 2030
sections.summary: States that total population is likely to be below 6.9 million by 2030, as indicated at last year's Committee of Supply.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As indicated at last year's Committee of Supply, our total population is likely to be below 6.9 million by 2030.

sections.label: Marriages, births and TFR
sections.summary: Reports 30,500 resident births, fewer resident marriages and births on average over five years, and a preliminary resident TFR of 0.97 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: At the core of our population vision are strong and stable families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We were also delighted to welcome 30,500 resident births.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Overall, however, there were fewer resident marriages and births annually on average over the last five years, as compared to the preceding five-year period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Preliminary estimates indicate a resident TFR of 0.97 in 2023, the first time it has dropped below 1.0.

sections.label: Paternity and infant care leave
sections.summary: States Government-Paid Paternity Leave was doubled to four weeks voluntarily and Unpaid Infant Care Leave raised to 12 days per parent yearly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To support working parents, we doubled Government-Paid Paternity Leave to four weeks on a voluntary basis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We also increased Unpaid Infant Care Leave to 12 days per parent per year in their child's first two years.

sections.label: HDB BTO supply
sections.summary: HDB has increased Build-to-Order supply and remains on track to launch 100,000 BTO flats from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Housing and Development Board (HDB) has ramped up Build-to-Order (BTO) supply and remains on track to launch 100,000 BTO flats from 2021 to 2025.

sections.label: Childcare fee caps lowered
sections.summary: MSF will lower childcare fee caps in Anchor and Partner Operator Preschools by $40 in 2025 and again in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Ministry for Social and Family Development (MSF) will lower childcare fee caps in Anchor and Partner Operator Preschools by $40 in 2025 and will lower them again in 2026.

sections.label: Baby and child healthcare coverage
sections.summary: All Singaporean babies are covered by MediShield Life from birth, parents receive a MediSave Grant, and children get subsidised vaccinations and screenings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In addition, all Singaporean babies are covered by MediShield Life from birth and their parents receive a MediSave Grant for newborns to help with the premiums.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And Singaporean children also enjoy fully-subsidised nationally-recommended childhood vaccinations and developmental screenings at polyclinics and GP clinics under the Community Health Assist Scheme.

sections.label: Government-Paid Paternity Leave increase
sections.summary: At Budget 2023, Government-Paid Paternity Leave was increased by two weeks from 1 January 2024 for fathers whose employers are ready.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: At Budget 2023, we increased Government-Paid Paternity Leave by two weeks effective from 1 January 2024, for fathers whose employers are ready to provide it.

sections.label: Question on mandating paternity leave
sections.summary: Mr Louis Ng asked when the additional paternity leave will be mandated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng asked when we will mandate this additional paternity leave.

sections.label: Exploring increased paid parental leave
sections.summary: Parents can return to work more easily once children are older, so paid parental leave is being actively explored for increase.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They can then return to work more easily once their children are older.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We are therefore actively exploring how to increase paid parental leave.

sections.label: BCA lactation room requirements
sections.summary: BCA has progressively enhanced building design requirements for lactation rooms and will continue to review them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Building and Construction Authority (BCA) has progressively enhanced the building design requirements for lactation rooms and will continue to review them.

sections.label: BCA Accessibility Fund co-funding
sections.summary: Building owners, lessors and lessees of eligible private developments may tap BCA's Accessibility Fund to co-fund construction of features and lactation pods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Building owners, lessors and lessees of eligible private developments may also tap on BCA’s Accessibility Fund to co-fund the construction costs of such features as well as lactation pods.

sections.label: New citizenships and PRs granted
sections.summary: In 2023, about 23,500 new citizenships were granted, including about 1,300 to children born overseas to Singaporean parents, plus about 34,500 new PRs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In 2023, we granted about 23,500 new citizenships, including about 1,300 to children born overseas to Singaporean parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We also granted about 34,500 new Permanent Residencies (PRs).

sections.label: Foreign workforce complements locals
sections.summary: Singapore lacks enough working locals for good economic growth, so it must remain open to a diverse foreign workforce that complements locals and fills manpower gaps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Even with immigrants, we do not have enough working locals to support continued good economic growth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We must, therefore, remain open to a diverse foreign workforce that complements the local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Foreign workers create value for Singaporeans, for example, by filling manpower gaps in sectors that Singaporeans are less keen to work in, or in disciplines where we may need more time to develop our own pool of local workers.

sections.label: SkillsFuture as social compact pillar
sections.summary: As detailed in the Forward Singapore report, SkillsFuture is a key pillar of our social compact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As detailed in the Forward Singapore report, SkillsFuture is a key pillar of our social compact.

sections.label: Made for Families co-funding ACP
sections.summary: The speaker calls on individuals, families, employers and communities to help shape a Singapore Made for Families, in relation to the Government's co-funding scheme for Assisted Conception Procedures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: While some of the bolder changes and mindset shifts may require more time, I call on everyone – individuals, families, employers and communities – to contribute towards shaping a Singapore that is Made for Families so that we can secure our future and thrive for years to come.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: This is in relation to the Government's co-funding scheme for Assisted Conception Procedures (ACP).

sections.label: Paternity leave mandate timeline
sections.summary: Asks whether a firm timeline can be given for mandating the extra two weeks of paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Rather than just have ASAP, whether we can have a firm timeline on when we will mandate the extra two weeks of paternity leave.

sections.label: Lactation rooms co-payment increase
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government can consider increasing the co-payment under the Accessibility Fund for lactation rooms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Second, on lactation rooms, we do have the Accessibility Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I am just wondering whether the Government can consider increasing the co-payment.

sections.label: Companies need time for paternity leave
sections.summary: States that Louis Ng is right that companies need time to implement paternity leave if it is made mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Mr Louis Ng is right that the companies do need time to implement it if we make paternity leave mandatory.

sections.label: MAS insurance fair practice guidelines
sections.summary: States that MAS' guidelines for insurance fair practice will soon address indiscriminate rejection of coverage applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS’) guidelines for insurance fair practice will soon address indiscriminate rejection of coverage applications.

sections.label: MAS list on discrimination
sections.summary: Asks whether MAS can provide a non-exhaustive list of illustrations showing what constitutes discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could MAS provide a non-exhaustive list of illustrations to show what constitutes discrimination?

sections.label: Addressing insurance discrimination, UNCRPD reservation
sections.summary: States that addressing systemic discrimination in insurance can build a more inclusive society and signal commitment to withdrawing the UNCRPD Article 25(e) reservation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By addressing the systemic discrimination in insurance, we can build a more inclusive and equitable society where all Singaporeans, regardless of disability, can access the financial protection they need to live with dignity and security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This will strongly signal the Government's commitment to work towards withdrawing its reservation of Article 25(e) of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD).

sections.label: Insurer assessment of disability applications
sections.summary: Insurers must objectively assess applications, but may still decline, charge higher premiums or set conditions for applicants with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Instead, insurers are expected to carry out an objective assessment of every application, based on reliable information or data relevant to the risk being insured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However even under the new proposed guidelines, insurers are not prohibited from declining applications, setting higher premiums or applying conditions in view of the risks presented by an applicant with a disability.

sections.label: Australian Scams Code Framework consultation
sections.summary: Australia's treasury issued a consultation paper on proposed industry codes obliging banks to detect, block, verify and trace scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In November last year, the Australian treasury issued a consultation paper on proposed industry codes for the private sector in combating scams – named the Scams Code Framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The extensive obligations on banks, include training of staff, detecting, blocking, verifying and tracing scams; and the need to implement anti-scam systems that are responsive to new products, services, designs and technologies.

sections.label: FIDReC adjudication monetary limit consultation
sections.summary: FIDReC announced a public consultation on raising its adjudication limit from $100,000 to $150,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, FIDReC announced in January a public consultation on raising its monetary limit in adjudication cases – from $100,000 to $150,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Should FIDReC consider raising its limit to $200,000, which is the daily threshold for PayNow transactions for consumers?

sections.label: Inappropriate differential treatment example
sections.summary: Rejecting an application solely on declared personal information like disability or medical condition is an example of inappropriate differential treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Under the proposed guidelines, an example of inappropriate differential treatment would be to reject an application solely on the basis of declared personal information, such as a disability or a medical condition.

sections.label: Explaining rejected or conditional applications
sections.summary: Insurers must explain the basis of decisions to reject or accept with condition, as set out in revised guidelines expected by mid-year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Where an application is rejected or accepted with condition, insurers are to properly explain to the applicant the basis of the decision.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This will also be set out in the revised guidelines, which we expect to issue by the middle of this year.

sections.label: Phishing and malware scam trends
sections.summary: Reported phishing cases and amounts lost fell in 2023, and MAS will work with banks to strengthen anti-scam controls and Money Lock.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The number of reported phishing cases in 2023 decreased by 16% compared to 2022, and the amounts lost decreased by 14%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The incidence of malware enabled scams has also reduced significantly after major retail banks introduced anti-malware security features on their banking apps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: MAS will build on this progress by continuing to work with banks to further strengthen anti-scam controls.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We will better safeguard funds by encouraging people to adopt Money Lock, and enhancing Money Lock's functionality.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: MAS is also working with banks to improve their fraud surveillance capabilities and to strengthen authentication measures at account logins and when making payment transactions.

sentences.text: Such a law could include publicly available registers of lobbyists, lobbying contact with political appointees, Members of Parliament, and very senior public servants, as well as board memberships of Members of Parliament.
